record.title: Axioms for physical reasoning: codifying the Seiberg-Witten solution in Lean
record.version: arXiv:2607.06379v1, submitted 2026-07-07; companion repository mrdouglasny/seiberg-witten (not inspected in this pass)
record.locator: HTML v1: Sec. 2 two kinds of formalization; Sec. 4.1 dictionary; Sec. 4.2 H0-H7; Sec. 4.4 what formalizing forces into the open; Sec. 5 checking the axioms; Appendices A-B
record.relevance: The clearest public discipline for separating named physical postulates from checked mathematics, with a working semantic-audit practice: dependency printing, numerical oracle, adversarial statement review, and vacuity hardening. Direct template for our audit procedure.
record.limits: Authors' report; repository and oracle scripts not inspected or rerun here. The physical postulates are argued for, not derived; their justification is external review plus numerics by the authors' own account.
design_principles: Physical postulates are named predicates carried in theorem types (H0-H7); the Lean `axiom` keyword carries only mathematics, so physics never hides in the trusted base (Sec. 2, 4.2, Appendix A).

A single dictionary maps each physical concept to a named mathematical object (e.g., PeriodChart.a/.aD/.tau as coupling; SymplecticReframing as duality); physics enters only through the dictionary (Sec. 4.1).
#print axioms reports the complete trusted base of any result; the genus-one uniqueness theorem's reported footprint is three logical axioms plus two classical covering axioms (Sec. 4.3).
Two kinds of formalization distinguished: proving existing rigorous statements vs. codifying trusted non-rigorous arguments (Sec. 2).
failure_modes_documented: Vacuous hypotheses: first-pass H3 ('there exists a lattice map equal to the Picard-Lefschetz transvection') was true by fiat; hardened to demand an actual deck transformation with covariant central charge. H2 hardened to demand a nonzero charge go massless; H5 pinned to 'exactly 2N' was unsatisfiable at rank 1 and corrected to 'order dividing 2N' with the u -> -u reflection as witness (Sec. 4.4).
A convenient falsehood refused by types: single-valued periods would be vacuous (bounded holomorphic map extends and is constant); data must live on the universal cover (Sec. 4.4).

Family-dependence trap: H6's instanton expansion with free coefficients fits any prepotential at fixed Lambda; content appears only as a weighted-homogeneity clause across the Lambda-family (Sec. 4.4). Heuristic recorded: for every existential inside a hypothesis, ask what stops the witness being reverse-engineered.

Adversarial review beat 62 passing numerical checks: a proposed axiom set failed statement-level review with three gaps (pointwise existence without holomorphic choice, missing boundary limits, an unlabelled parabolic slot); a hyperbolic matrix briefly occupied a parabolic slot passing every property the proofs consumed (Sec. 5, 'Validating a transcription').

The checking apparatus itself erred twice (fractional power on the wrong branch; cycle normalization off by a factor of two), caught by anchor values such as lambda(i)=1/2 before agreeing with Lean (Sec. 5, oracle paragraph).
record.verification_protocol_as_published: Cheapest first: (1) independent numerical oracle in mpmath/numpy sharing no code or authorship with Lean - 9 suites, 278 checks at 30-40 digit precision; authors call a numerical pass 'necessary, not sufficient'; (2) cross-model and self-review against pinned sources, separating 'is it proved?', 'does it say what the source says?', and 'can the intended theorems be derived from it?'; (3) transcription validation with four checks - instantiation, oracle, agreement with independently proved results, adversarial content; (4) the physicist's triangle: independent routes to the same quantity (perturbation theory, Nekrasov instantons, exact periods) attached as a cross-check rather than asserted (Sec. 5).
record.authors_claim: AI's characteristic error in physics derivations is 'a hallucinated assumption, an unphysical premise or a dropped subtlety presented as if derived' (Sec. 1) - the error class our audit targets.
record.proof_status: Authors report sorry-free genus-one theorems with printed axiom footprints; not rebuilt here.
open_questions: Inspect mrdouglasny/seiberg-witten: pin commit, read validate_singcount.py and oracle suites, verify the printed axiom footprints by building.

record.title: Dynamical locality of the free scalar field
record.section_locator: Abstract; Sec. 4, Theorem 4.3 and adjacent construction/proof, lines 406-422 in arXiv HTML

The theorem is specific to that quotient model and those categories.
record.conclusion: The quotient massless scalar theory is dynamically local in Loc_0 for all spacetime dimensions n>=2 and in Loc for n>=3, but not in Loc at n=2. The authors exhibit the two-dimensional disconnected-spacetime topological obstruction; they conjecture adding topological charge as background may address it. This is a model/domain-specific locality result, not a universal claim about local events.
record.proof_status: Theorem 4.3 statement and explanatory derivation inspected; no independent reproduction.

The comparison target is kinematic versus dynamical localization as defined in the Fewster–Verch framework.
record.open_questions: The paper identifies topological charge as a conjectural diagnosis of the two-dimensional failure; keep the authors' conjecture separate from theorem content.
record.relevance: Concrete counterexample to treating kinematic and dynamical localization as automatically identical.
record.limits: Massless scalar quotient model only; do not generalize the dimensional exception to all AQFTs.

record.title: Gravity, Entropy, and Cosmology: In Search of Clarity
record.version: arXiv:0907.0659v1 (2009-07-03); British Journal for the Philosophy of Science 61(3) (2010), pp. 513-540
record.locators: Secs. 2-4, 8-10 of primary HTML read by a subsequent reviewer in this task; key distinctions at Sec. 3 and revised principles/conclusion at Sec. 10. Original worker's earlier screening was abstract-level.
record.assumptions: Distinguishes gravity's dynamical effects on material macrostates from entropy attributed to gravitational field degrees of freedom. Argues in relevant cosmological regimes that local matter entropy and radiation, expansion-driven departure from equilibrium, and gravitational dynamics must be considered; black-hole entropy is a special case. Scope is the author's statistical-mechanical analysis, not a general quantum-gravity derivation.
record.conclusion: Wallace argues that collapse need not increase the collapsing matter's entropy: in his model discussion the matter's entropy can decrease while heat/radiation transfer increases total entropy. He says gravitational collapse is not generally the source of local second-law behavior; expansion and nuclear fusion matter to his account. He criticizes Earman's limitations as too strong because gravity can affect material statistical mechanics through dynamics even when field entropy is neglected. This is a substantive counterpoint, not a final resolution of the Past Hypothesis or a universal entropy formula.
record.proof_status: Primary arXiv HTML sections 2-4 and 8-10 read in a subsequent reviewer pass after the initial abstract-only record; calculations and wider empirical claims not independently reproduced.
record.dependencies: Classical statistical mechanics of gravitating matter, expanding-universe thermodynamics, matter/radiation entropy, and distinctions between field entropy and dynamical influence.
record.open_questions: Which parts of Wallace's classical account generalize to broader relativistic/quantum cosmological models; what entropy functional is appropriate for the initial universe; how does the account compare to later gravitational entropy proposals?
record.relevance: Detailed adversarial counterpoint to both a simplistic Weyl=entropy identification and the claim that Earman's critique rules out cosmological entropy reasoning; also shows why gravitational dynamics can matter without assigning an entropy to the gravitational field.
record.limits: This is the author's argument in a bounded 2009 treatment; it does not settle all gravitational-entropy questions or establish a unique cosmological entropy. No independent calculation or contemporary model audit.

record.title: Smoothness of time functions and the metric splitting of globally hyperbolic spacetimes
record.version: arXiv gr-qc/0401112v3 (15 Feb 2005); Commun. Math. Phys. 257 (2005), 43–50
record.relevance: Sharp existence result linking global hyperbolicity to a smooth Cauchy temporal function and orthogonal product splitting.

record.assumptions: Time-oriented smooth Lorentzian spacetime; Theorem 1.1 assumes global hyperbolicity. Theorem 1.2 assumes an existing continuous time function.

Any spacetime admitting a time function admits a temporal function. The theorem supplies existence, not a unique or physically preferred foliation.

record.title: Can Bohmian mechanics be made relativistic?
record.relevance: Central modern statement of the Bohmian foliation problem and the main escape route: instead of positing a preferred foliation as extra structure, let it be covariantly determined by the wave function; authors argue such theories 'seem to qualify as fundamentally Lorentz invariant'.
record.limits: Full text read at argument level; Sec. 6 quantum equilibrium skimmed, not re-derived.
record.section_locator: Read via ar5iv HTML (50,983 chars). Sec. 2 'Bohmian theories in relativistic space-time'; Sec. 3 geometry of foliations (incl. the integrable-vector-field construction where leaves are normal to n only when n is integrable); Sec. 4 'Lorentz invariance'; Sec. 5 generalizations; Sec. 7 'Discussion'.
record.assumptions: Relativistic Bohmian particle dynamics for N>1 needs a foliation; the question is its status: posited (hero) vs covariantly wave-function-determined; quantum equilibrium assumed for empirical equivalence.
record.conclusion: Authors' claim: positing a foliation looks like a violation of fundamental Lorentz invariance, but a wave-function-determined foliation yields Bohmian theories that arguably remain fundamentally Lorentz invariant; conclusion is hedged ('seem to qualify').
record.proof_status: Conceptual/geometric construction with technical sections; main conclusion is explicitly evaluative, not a theorem. Not reproduced.
record.open_questions: Whether wave-function-determined foliations are dynamically stable under interactions; whether 'fundamental Lorentz invariance' under their definition matches philosophical standards for Lorentz invariance.
record.paper_claim_vs_established: Foliation as extra structure for N>1 = consensus in the Bohmian literature. 'Covariantly wave-function-determined foliation preserves fundamental Lorentz invariance' = the authors' hedged claim, not an established result. Whether this blocks Rietdijk-Putnam-style inference = our note.

record.title: A Classical Sequential Growth Dynamics for Causal Sets
record.version: arXiv:gr-qc/9904062v3 (revised 26 Jun 2004; SU-GP-99/4-1); Phys. Rev. D 61, 024002 (2000); doi 10.1103/PhysRevD.61.024002. Text from ar5iv render; key formulas cross-checked against the v3 LaTeX source (e-print dated 2004-06-26).
record.section_locator: Sec. 1.1 (natural labeling, fictitious external time); Sec. 3 (internal temporality, discrete general covariance, Bell causality Eq. (2), Markov sum rule); Sec. 4 (Lemmas 1-4, Eqs. (3)-(13), Claims on inequalities); Sec. 4.4 (verification, Eqs. (14)-(15)); Sec. 5 (Eqs. (17)-(18), Prob_N(C)=W(C)P(C)); Sec. 7 (open questions); Appendix Lemmas 5-6. The paper has no numbered theorem; the main result is the derivation in Sec. 4.
record.assumptions: Markov transition probabilities; internal temporality (births to the future of or unrelated to existing elements; natural labelling); discrete general covariance (path independence of the product of transition probabilities); Bell causality (ratio of sibling transition probabilities depends only on the union of precursor sets); Markov sum rule; genericity: no transition probability vanishes (Sec. 4); elements counted as distinguishable (sum-rule multiplicities).
record.conclusion: Authors' derivation: under those conditions the transition probability is alpha_n = lambda(w,m)/lambda(n,0) with lambda(w,m)=sum_{k=m}^{w} C(w-m,w-k) t_k, free parameters t_n>=0, t_0=1 (equivalently q_n with q_n^-1 = sum C(n,k) t_k); transitive percolation is t_n=t^n. Label-independent formation weight P(C)=prod_x lambda(w(x),m(x))/prod_j lambda(j,0). Authors state that labels are fictitious/gauge and that statements such as 'when the causet had 8 elements it was a chain' are meaningless; they describe the phenomenological passage of time as a manifestation of growth. These are the authors' interpretive claims, not consequences of the mathematics.
record.proof_status: Hand derivation in the paper (Lemmas 1-6 with proofs); no formal or machine verification. Not independently re-derived here beyond reading; the n<=5 finite check in knowledge/defeat-search/csg_ancillarity_check.py (coordinator) is exact rational arithmetic for two parameter vectors through n=5, not a general proof or an observer model. Coordinator re-ran it on 2026-10-19.
dependencies: Markovian sequential growth; Kleitman-Rothschild entropy problem motivation; Sorkin quantum measure (gr-qc/9401003) for the quantum extension, not used
open_questions: Can Bell causality be formulated without a birth sequence? (Sec. 7, authors)
Are all meaningful assertions combinations of partial-stem occurrence? (conjecture, Sec. 5/7, authors)
Non-generic cases with vanishing transition probabilities (originary models) left open by the authors
Equation numbers are those of the ar5iv/LaTeXML v3 render; the journal numbering was not checked.
record.relevance: Anchor for growth-model comparison (candidate A): defines the label-independence and Bell-causality conditions and the transition probabilities.
record.limits: Classical model family; no observers, records or clock construction in the paper; passage language is interpretive. Text extraction flattens sub/superscripts, so formulas were verified against LaTeX for (6),(7),(12),(17) and P(C_n)=W p^L q^(C(n,2)-R).

record.title: What becomes of a causal set
record.version: arXiv:1502.00018v1 (30 Jan 2015); 'forthcoming in the British Journal for the Philosophy of Science' per arXiv comments (publication details not checked). Text from ar5iv render.
record.section_locator: Sec. 3 'Facing the same dilemma?' (Stein's theorem, counterexample causet R, non-Hegelian subsets); Sec. 4 'Taking growth seriously' (CSG as tenseless history space, localized becoming, label time, gauge-invariant growth, posts, Fig. 3); Sec. 5 conclusion. No numbered theorems.
record.assumptions: Causet = locally finite partial order (reflexive convention); Stein-style becoming as a binary relation R 'definite as of' that is reflexive, non-trivial, non-universal, automorphism-invariant; CSG dynamics with discrete general covariance; the quotient-by-relabelling measure of Brightwell et al. 2003; identity conditions of events (for coherence of the 'exotic' becoming).
record.conclusion: Authors' claims: (i) the analogue of Stein's theorem is false in CST (counterexample causet with b,c spacelike related; R includes <b,c> and <c,b> without collapsing to universal); but non-Hegelian subsets large enough for a global present are non-generic, and regular ones would violate Lorentz invariance, so CST 'embraces' the dilemma; (ii) CSG is compatible with a tenseless history-space reading; (iii) localized/observer-dependent becoming is available but has Minkowski analogues; (iv) a novel global, objective but ontologically indeterminate 'becoming' (cardinality grows, which elements exist at a stage is not determinate) is compatible with CST, at radical metaphysical cost (vague existence, indeterminate past). Authors do not claim it is physically established.
record.proof_status: Informal philosophical argument with one explicit counterexample (checkable by hand); no formal proof. Quoted Meyer non-Hegelian-pair estimate is an unpublished result cited by the authors, unread.
dependencies: Huggett 2014, Pooley 2013, Earman 2008, Arageorgis 2012, Dowker 2014 as cited, all unread
open_questions: Whether the cardinality-only 'becoming' is coherent depends on event identity conditions (authors)
Whether the measure being defined only on Omega(infinity) makes the infinite end state prior to the growth (authors raise it)
Whether non-Hegelian-subset statistics hold for realistic causets (only Meyer's unpublished 1+1 estimate cited)
record.relevance: Closest philosophical prior art for candidate A and for any claim that causal-set growth supplies objective passage.
record.limits: Philosophy-of-physics argument; the Stein-analogue statement is in prose (Sec. 3), not a theorem with proof. The paper's Stein statement is paraphrased from Stein 1991 and was not checked against it. Coordinator directly checked Secs. 3-4 in the versioned HTML; the prose Stein reconstruction must not be reused as a validated primary theorem (transitivity/strict-versus-reflexive qualifications unresolved).
